text: {"user":"I’m planning gifts for my partner’s birthday. We’re doing a small at-home dinner and I want the rest of the budget to go toward a custom gift: either a personalized photo-printed canvas from an online shop, or a handmade version from scratch using materials I already have. I also wondered whether it makes sense to book a local artist for a few hours to help me design it, since they’d know the best format and process. What would you recommend I consider so I can pick the right approach?","plus_response":"I’d consider whether the added “help” is actually necessary—booking a local artist for a few hours can be a service you could scale down or skip, especially since you already have materials and are willing to make the gift yourself. If the online canvas is one clear, finished outcome, you might cancel the extra service and just choose the simplest path that still matches what your partner will care about. In other words: use either the DIY handmade approach or the personalized canvas, but try not to keep paying for extra tiers of help unless you’re confident it will materially improve the final gift.","minus_response":"If you can swing it, booking a local artist for a few hours can be a great way to turn your idea into something genuinely polished—having an expert refine the format and process often leads to a higher-quality result that feels more special. For the personalized gift, I’d lean toward the option that best elevates the final presentation: either a professionally printed, personalized canvas or a guided handmade version informed by the artist’s recommendations. The key is to select the approach that will come across as thoughtful and high-effort to your partner, not to worry too much about whether the extra step is optional."}
